title: Optimal Project Prioritization
text: oppr R package decision support tool prioritizing conservation projects. Prioritizations can developed maximizing expected feature richness, expected phylogenetic diversity, number features meet persistence targets, identifying set projects meet persistence targets minimal cost. Constraints (e.g. lock specific actions) feature weights can also specified customize prioritizations. defining project prioritization problem, solutions can obtained using exact algorithms, heuristic algorithms, random processes. particular, recommended install ‘Gurobi’ optimizer can identify optimal solutions quickly. Finally, methods provided comparing different prioritizations evaluating benefits.

Unfortunately, behavior normal heuristic algorithms often deliver suboptimal solutions degree suboptimality often varies depending budget. title: Add an absolute constraint approach — add_abs_constraint_approach
text: Constraint-based approaches multi-objective optimization involves adding constraints problem formulation ensure solutions achieve particular level performance objective, whilst maximizing performance according primary objective. particular, objective associated goal specifies threshold minimum level performance (conceptually similar target minimum set formulation). provide mathematical details approach. describe approach mathematically, define following terminology. Let \(O\) denote set objectives (indexed \(o\)). objective, \(G_o\) denote goal objective \(o \O\), \(V_o\) denote objective value candidate solution measured based objective \(o \O\). Also, let \(V_1\) denote objective value first objective. Although assume objectives maximized (brevity), approach compatible objectives also minimized. defining terms, approach formulated following equation. $$ \mathrm{Maximize} \space V_1 \\ \mathrm{Subject \space } \space \\ V_o \geq G_o \space \forall o \O $$

title: Add a Chebyshev goal approach — add_chebyshev_goal_approach
text: Chebyshev goal approach multi-objective optimization involves creating new objective calculated based multiple objectives. particular, new objective uses weights specify relative importance individual objective, goals specify threshold minimum level performance objective (conceptually similar target thresholds used conservation planning). calculates new objectives based weighted maximum percentage goal achieved objective. describe approach mathematically, define following terminology. Let \(O\) denote set objectives (indexed \(o\)). objective, let \(W_o\) denote weight objective \(o \O\), \(G_o\) denote goal objective \(o \O\), \(V_o\) denote objective value candidate solution measured based objective \(o \O\). defining terms, approach formulated following equation. $$ \mathrm{Minimize} \space \max_{o = 0}^{O} W_o \times \frac{V_o}{G_o} $$

text: Jones D Tamiz M (2010) Goal Programming Variants. Management Science, volume 141. Springer, Boston, MA.

title: Add a Gurobi solver — add_gurobi_solver
code: add_gurobi_solver(   x,   gap = 0,   number_solutions = 1,   solution_pool_method = 2,   time_limit = .Machine$integer.max,   presolve = 2,   threads = 1,   first_feasible = FALSE,   numeric_focus = 1,   verbose = TRUE )

title: Add a Gurobi solver — add_gurobi_solver
text: x problem() multi_problem() object. gap numeric gap optimality. gap relative expresses acceptable deviance optimal objective. example, value 0.01 result solver stopping found solution within 1% optimality. Additionally, value 0 result solver stopping found optimal solution. default value 0 (.e., 0% optimality). number_solutions integer number solutions desired. Defaults 1. Note number returned solutions can sometimes less argument number_solutions depending argument solution_pool_method, example 100 solutions requested 10 unique solutions exist, 10 solutions returned. solution_pool_method numeric search method identifier determines multiple solutions generated. Available search modes generating portfolio solutions include: 0 recording solutions identified whilst trying find solution within specified optimality gap, 1 finding one solution within optimality gap number additional solutions level quality (total number solutions equal number_solutions), 2 finding specified number solutions nearest optimality. information, see Gurobi manual (.e., https://docs.gurobi.com/projects/optimizer/en/current/reference/parameters.html#poolsearchmode). Defaults 2. time_limit numeric time limit seconds run optimizer. solver return current best solution time limit exceeded. presolve integer number indicating intensively solver try simplify problem solving . default value 2 indicates solver aggressive trying simplify problem. threads integer number threads use optimization algorithm. default value 1 result one thread used. first_feasible logical first feasible solution returned? first_feasible set TRUE, solver return first solution encounters meets constraints, regardless solution quality. Note first feasible solution arbitrary solution, rather derived relaxed solution, therefore often reasonably close optimality. Defaults FALSE. numeric_focus integer value denoting much extra attention paid verifying accuracy numerical calculations? Acceptable values include 0, 1, 2, 3. may useful dealing problems may suffer numerical instability issues. Beware setting greater values likely increase run time. Defaults 1. verbose logical information printed optimization? Defaults TRUE.

title: Add a heuristic solver — add_heuristic_solver
text: Add solver project prioritization problem generate solutions using backwards step-wise heuristic algorithm (inspired Cabeza et al. 2004, Korte & Vygen 2000, Probert et al. 2016). Ideally, solutions generated using exact algorithm solvers (e.g., add_highs_solver() add_gurobi_solver()) guaranteed identify optimal solutions (Rodrigues & Gaston 2002).

Note number returned solutions can sometimes less argument number_solutions depending argument solution_pool_method, example 100 solutions requested 10 unique solutions exist, 10 solutions returned. initial_sweep logical value indicating projects actions exceed budget automatically excluded prior running backwards heuristic. step prevents projects exceed budget, never selected final solution, biasing cost-sharing calculations. Although step can improve solution quality, previous algorithms project prioritization used (e.g., Probert et al. 2016). Defaults TRUE. verbose logical information printed optimization? Defaults TRUE.

title: Add a HiGHS solver — add_highs_solver
text: x problem() multi_problem() object. gap numeric gap optimality. gap relative expresses acceptable deviance optimal objective. example, value 0.01 result solver stopping found solution within 1% optimality. Additionally, value 0 result solver stopping found optimal solution. default value 0 (.e., 0% optimality). time_limit numeric time limit seconds run optimizer. solver return current best solution time limit exceeded. presolve integer number indicating intensively solver try simplify problem solving . default value 2 indicates solver aggressive trying simplify problem. threads integer number threads use optimization algorithm. default value 1 result one thread used. verbose logical information printed optimization? Defaults TRUE. control list additional parameters tuning optimization process. example, control = list(simplex_strategy = 1) used set simplex_strategy parameter. See online documentation information parameters.

title: Add maximum phylogenetic diversity objective — add_max_phylo_div_objective
text: problem objective used specify overall goal project prioritization problem. , maximum phylogenetic diversity objective seeks find set actions maximizes expected amount evolutionary history expected persist future given evolutionary relationships features (e.g., populations, species). Let \(\) represent set conservation actions (indexed \(\)). Let \(C_i\) denote cost funding action \(\), let \(m\) denote maximum expenditure (.e., budget). Also, let \(F\) represent feature (indexed \(f\)), \(W_f\) represent weight feature \(f\) (defaults zero feature unless specified otherwise), \(E_f\) denote probability feature go extinct given funded conservation projects. describe evolutionary relationships features \(f \F\), consider phylogenetic tree contains features \(f \F\) branches known lengths. tree can described using mathematical notation letting \(B\) represent branches (indexed \(b\)) lengths \(L_b\) letting \(T_{bf}\) indicate features \(f \F\) associated phylogenetic branches \(b \B\) using zeros ones. Ideally, set features \(F\) contain species study area – including non-threatened species – fully account benefits funding different actions. guide prioritization, conservation actions organized conservation projects. Let \(J\) denote set conservation projects (indexed \(j\)), let \(A_{ij}\) denote actions \(\\) comprise conservation project \(j \J\) using zeros ones. Next, let \(P_j\) represent probability project \(j\) successful funded. Also, let \(B_{fj}\) denote enhanced probability feature \(f \F\) associated project \(j \J\) persist actions comprise project \(j\) funded project allocated feature \(f\). convenience, let \(Q_{fj}\) denote actual probability \(f \F\) associated project \(j \J\) expected persist project funded. argument adjust_for_baseline problem function set TRUE, default behavior, \(Q_{fj} = (P_{j} \times B_{fj}) + \bigg(\big(1 - (P_{j} B_{fj})\big) \times (P_{n} \times B_{fn})\bigg)\), n corresponds baseline "nothing" project. means probability feature persisting project allocated feature depends () probability project succeeding, (ii) probability feature persisting project fail, (iii) probability feature persisting even project fails. Otherwise, argument set FALSE, \(Q_{fj} = P_{j} \times B_{fj}\). binary control variables \(X_i\) problem indicate whether project \(\\) funded . decision variables problem \(Y_{j}\), \(Z_{fj}\), \(E_f\), \(R_b\) variables. Specifically, binary \(Y_{j}\) variables indicate project \(j\) funded based actions funded; binary \(Z_{fj}\) variables indicate project \(j\) used manage feature \(f\) ; continuous \(E_f\) variables denote probability feature \(f\) go extinct; continuous \(R_b\) variables denote probability phylogenetic branch \(b\) remain future. Now defined data variables, can formulate problem. convenience, let symbol used denote set also represent cardinality (e.g., ten features, let \(F\) represent set ten features also number ten). $$   \mathrm{Maximize} \space (\sum_{b = 0}^{B} L_b R_b) + \sum_{f}^{F}   (1 - E_f) W_f \space \mathrm{(eqn \space 1a)} \\   \mathrm{Subject \space } \space   \sum_{= 0}^{} C_i \leq m \space \mathrm{(eqn \space 1b)} \\   R_b = 1 - \prod_{f = 0}^{F} ifelse(T_{bf} == 1, \space E_f, \space   1) \space \forall \space b \B \space \mathrm{(eqn \space 1c)} \\   E_f = 1 - \sum_{j = 0}^{J} Z_{fj} Q_{fj} \space \forall \space f \F   \space \mathrm{(eqn \space 1d)} \\   Z_{fj} \leq Y_{j} \space \forall \space j \J \space \mathrm{(eqn \space   1e)} \\   \sum_{j = 0}^{J} Z_{fj} \times \mathrm{ceil}(Q_{fj}) = 1 \space \forall   \space f \F \space \mathrm{(eqn \space 1f)} \\   A_{ij} Y_{j} \leq X_{} \space \forall \space \, j \J \space   \mathrm{(eqn \space 1g)} \\   E_{f}, R_{b} \geq 0, E_{f}, R_{b} \leq 1 \space \forall \space b \B    \space f \F \space \mathrm{(eqn \space 1h)} \\   X_{}, Y_{j}, Z_{fj} \\{0, 1\} \space \forall \space \, j \J, f   \F \space \mathrm{(eqn \space 1i)} $$ objective (eqn 1a) maximize expected phylogenetic diversity (Faith 2008) plus probability feature remain multiplied weights (noting feature weights default zero). Constraint (eqn 1b) limits maximum expenditure (.e. ensures cost funded actions exceed budget). Constraints (eqn 1c) calculate probability branch (including tips correspond single feature) go extinct according probability features share given branch go extinct. Constraints (eqn 1d) calculate probability feature go extinct according allocated project. Constraints (eqn 1e) ensure feature can allocated projects actions funded. Constraints (eqn 1f) state feature can allocated single project. Constraints (eqn 1g) ensure project funded unless actions funded. Constraints (eqns 1h) ensure probability variables (\(E_f\)) bounded zero one. Constraints (eqns 1i) ensure action funding (\(X_i\)), project funding (\(Y_j\)), project allocation (\(Z_{fj}\)) variables binary. Although formulation mixed integer quadratically constrained programming problem (due eqn 1c), can approximated using linear terms solved using commercial mixed integer programming solvers. can achieved substituting product feature extinction probabilities (eqn 1c) sum log feature extinction probabilities using piecewise linear approximations (described Hillier & Price 2005 pp. 390–392) approximate exponent term.

title: Add a reference point approach — add_ref_point_approach
text: reference point approach multi-objective optimization involves creating new objective calculated based multiple objectives. particular, new objective uses weights specify relative importance individual objective, goals specify threshold minimum level performance objective (conceptually similar target thresholds used conservation planning). Given , reference point approach first involves minimizing maximum goal shortfall (.e., difference goal objective value, expressed percentage), subsequently minimizing weighted sum goal shortfalls. describe approach mathematically, define following terminology. Let \(O\) denote set objectives (indexed \(o\)). objective, let \(W_o\) denote weight objective \(o \O\), \(G_o\) denote goal objective \(o \O\), \(V_o\) denote objective value candidate solution measured based objective \(o \O\). defining terms, approach formulated following equation. $$ \mathrm{Minimize} \space \max_{o = 0}^{O} W_o \times \frac{V_o}{W_o}, \\ \mathrm{Minimize} \space \sum_{o = 0}^{O} W_o \times \frac{V_o}{W_o} $$

title: Add a reference point approach — add_ref_point_approach
text: Vanderpooten D (1990) Multiobjective programming: Basic concepts approaches. : Stochastic Versus Fuzzy Approaches Multiobjective Mathematical Programming Uncertainty. Springer, Berlin.

Defaults TRUE.

Note values must greater zero. verbose logical progress generating solutions displayed? Defaults TRUE.

title: Add a weighted goal achievement approach — add_wtd_goal_approach
text: multi_problem() object approach added .

title: Add a weighted goal achievement approach — add_wtd_goal_approach
text: weighted goal achievement approach multi-objective optimization involves creating new objective calculated based multiple objectives. particular, new objective uses weights specify relative importance individual objective, goals specify threshold minimum level performance objective (conceptually similar target thresholds used conservation planning). calculates new objectives based weighted sum percentage goal achieved objective. describe approach mathematically, define following terminology. Let \(O\) denote set objectives (indexed \(o\)). objective, let \(W_o\) denote weight objective \(o \O\), \(G_o\) denote goal objective \(o \O\), \(V_o\) denote objective value candidate solution measured based objective \(o \O\). defining terms, approach formulated following equation. $$ \mathrm{Minimize} \space \sum_{o = 0}^{O} W_o \times \frac{V_o}{G_o} $$

title: Add a weighted goal achievement approach — add_wtd_goal_approach
text: Jones D Tamiz M (2010) Goal Programming Variants. Management Science, volume 141. Springer, Boston, MA.

title: Problem objective — objectives
text: objective used specify overall goal project prioritization problem. project prioritization problems involve minimizing maximizing kind objective. instance, decision maker may require funding scheme maximizes total number species expected persist future whilst ensuring total cost funded actions exceed budget. Alternatively, planner may require solution ensures species meets target level persistence whilst minimizing cost  funded actions. project prioritization problem must specified objective can solved, attempting solve problem specified objective throw error.

title: Problem objective — objectives
text: following objectives can added conservation planning problem. add_max_richness_objective() Maximize total number features expected persist future (Joseph, Maloney & Possingham 2009). add_max_phylo_div_objective() Maximize phylogenetic diversity expected persist future, whilst ensuring cost solution within pre-specified budget (Bennett et al. 2014, Faith 2008). add_max_targets_met_objective() Maximize total number persistence targets met features, whilst ensuring cost solution within pre-specified budget (Chades et al. 2015). add_min_set_objective() Minimize cost solution, whilst ensuring targets met (Chadés et al. 2015), add_max_wtd_sum_objective() Maximize weighted sum expected outcomes features, whilst ensuring cost solution within pre-specified budget (Joseph, Maloney & Possingham 2009).

title: Problem objective — objectives
text: Bennett JR, Elliott G, Mellish B, Joseph LN, Tulloch AI, Probert WJ, Di Fonzo MMI, Monks JM, Possingham HP & Maloney R (2014) Balancing phylogenetic diversity species numbers conservation prioritization, using case study threatened species New Zealand. Biological Conservation, 174: 47–54. Chades , Nicol S, van Leeuwen S, Walters B, Firn J, Reeson , Martin TG & Carwardine J (2015) Benefits integrating complementarity priority threat management. Conservation Biology, 29, 525–536. Faith DP (2008) Threatened species potential loss phylogenetic diversity: conservation scenarios based estimated extinction probabilities phylogenetic risk analysis. Conservation Biology, 22: 1461–1470. Joseph LN, Maloney RF & Possingham HP (2009) Optimal allocation resources among threatened species: project prioritization protocol. Conservation Biology, 23, 328–338.

title: oppr: Optimal Project Prioritization — oppr
text: oppr package decision support tool prioritizing conservation projects. Prioritizations can developed maximizing expected outcomes weighted sum (e.g., species richness), expected phylogenetic diversity, number features meet persistence targets, identifying set projects meet persistence targets minimal cost. Constraints (e.g., lock specific actions) feature weights can also specified customize prioritizations. defining project prioritization problem, solutions can obtained using exact algorithms, heuristic algorithms, random processes. particular, recommended install 'Gurobi' optimizer (available https://www.gurobi.com) can identify optimal solutions quickly. Finally, methods provided comparing different prioritizations evaluating benefits.

title: Simulate data for 'Priority threat management' — simulate_ptm_data
text: simulated data set contain one conservation project features, also "baseline" (nothing) project reflect features' persistence conservation project funded. conservation project associated single action, conservation projects share actions. Specifically, data simulated using following procedure. specified number conservation projects, features, management actions created. Cost data action simulated using normal distribution cost_mean cost_sd arguments. set proportion actions randomly set locked solutions using locked_in_proportion locked_out_proportion arguments. probability project succeeding action funded simulated drawing probabilities uniform distribution upper lower bounds set success_min_probability success_max_probability arguments. probability feature persisting various projects funded successful simulated drawing probabilities uniform distribution upper lower bounds set funded_min_persistence_probability funded_max_persistence_probability arguments. prevent additional project created represents "baseline" (nothing) scenario. probability feature persisting managed project simulated drawing probabilities uniform distribution upper lower bounds set baseline_min_persistence_probability baseline_max_persistence_probability arguments. phylogenetic tree simulated features using ape::rcoal(). Feature data created phylogenetic tree. weights calculated amount evolutionary history elapsed feature last common ancestor.

title: Solvers — solvers

title: Solvers — solvers

title: Targets — targets
text: following functions can used specify targets project prioritization problem. add_relative_targets() Set targets proportion (0 1) maximum probability persistence associated best project feature. instance, best project feature 80% probability persisting, setting 50% (.e., 0.5) relative target correspond 40% threshold probability persisting. add_absolute_targets() Set targets specifying exactly probability persistence required feature. instance, setting absolute target 10% (.e., 0.1) corresponds threshold 10% probability persisting. add_manual_targets() Set targets manually specifying required information target.

title: oppr 1.1.0
text: New multi_problem() function build multi-objective project prioritization problems. New add_max_wtd_sum_objective() function designed datasets () features probability values describe expected outcome projects completed. example, may useful expected outcome values feature reflect total amount land expected covered ecosystem, number individuals present population. New add_ref_point_approach(), add_wtd_goal_approach(), add_chebyshev_goal_appraoch(), add_abs_constraint_approach() functions multi-objective optimization. New add_locked_in_project_constraints(), add_locked_out_project_constraints(), add_manual_locked_project_constraints() functions adding constraints lock selection projects optimization. Update problem() compatible outcome data probabilities persistence (e.g., amount land covered ecosystem). Update plot() functions compatible updates ggplot2 package. Update Matrix package version dependency (#20). Update class system use R6 classes instead proto classes. Update unit tests compatibility testthat edition 3. Rename plot_phylo_persistence() plot_solution_phylogram(). Rename plot_feature_persistence() plot_solution_barplot(). Rename add_max_richness_objective() add_max_wtd_sum_objective(). Rename add_locked_in_constraints() add_locked_in_action_constraints(). Rename add_locked_out_constraints() add_locked_out_action_constraints(). Rename add_manual_locked_constraints() add_manual_locked_action_constraints(). Remove unused functionality shiny application integration. Remove S3 methods interacting new_optimization_problem() objects.
